prompt: Use case: stylized-concept with realistic animal anatomy and photoreal fantasy materials. Make ONE contact plate of THREE DISTINCT LEGENDARY CREATURE CONCEPTS for the SAME species, three columns A,B,C with two rows. Row1 each concept faces towards the viewer with substantial side profile; row2 show the corresponding SAME concept facing away. Camera looks down approximately30degrees from horizontal, near-orthographic long lens, model yaw towards/away approximately±34degrees from side profile. Whole creature INCLUDING tail, ears, palms, extended membranes and magic signature must fit each cell with ample margins. Plain light neutral grey ground, no landscape, text, grid labels, environment or interface. Adult elder creatures, NEVER cute juvenile toys. Maintain recognisable natural family, ancient wisdom/power, wear/scars and bold distinctive silhouette, not just scale. Each column must actually differ in its PRIMARY signature; age-grizzle is not the signature. Ed's rule fit+variety: crystal/flame/spirit-wings permitted when justified, no shared legendary uniform. Optional offerings physically fit the animal. Use no generic crown on every concept. Species: hedgehog. Area story: Hazel forest: short grass, brown ground lumps and red-berried shrubs, crooked many-branched trees. Concept A (left): The Bramble Bastion: low enormous European hedgehog with long pointed furry snout and a dorsal mantle of huge thick age-weathered spines, some broken and regrown, resembling a defensive lance forest; a few tiny warm lights only at oldest quill tips, not body-covering crystal armour. Feet short, no quills on face/belly. Concept B (middle): The Berry Offering Keeper: old low hedgehog with layered natural spines holding several red berry sprigs and dry hazel leaves as offerings, silver muzzle and a worn notch on one ear; a single translucent red berry larger than the rest glows gently within the spine mantle, no whole trees. Concept C (right): The Shielding Curl: huge hedgehog half-curled protectively, recognisable face and feet still visible; immense spines fan backwards into a crescent shell of warm pale light following actual spine roots, weathered bristles and old scars. No free-floating eye halo or wings.
